title: Shadow Evals Dashboard — UX Notes (IA, comparisons, terminology)
content:
Working doc — PM/Design collaboration notes for “Shadow Evals” dashboard in Redwood Console.

Context
- Shadow Traffic capability mirrors a sampled subset of production-shaped requests to one or more “shadow targets” and records quality + perf metrics.
- Console dashboard must support: (1) daily regression detection, (2) rollout/canary gating decisions, (3) post-incident analysis (what happened, where, which policy/target).
- Primary constraint to keep reinforcing in UI copy: shadowing never blocks and never changes end-user responses; shadow failures should not page customers unless they opted into gating.

Attendees / inputs considered
- PM: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (rollout policies)
- Design: Kenji Nakamura (Rollouts UX), Alicia Perez (Dashboards)
- Eng consult: Chloe Martin (Console backend), Jin Woo Park (metrics), Logan Wright (telemetry), Jonas Weber (evals)

Customer personas / top jobs-to-be-done
1) Platform/ML engineer upgrading model version
- Wants “Is candidate better than baseline on our real traffic?”
- Wants fast, defensible answer + drill-down to examples.
2) SRE / on-call investigating GPU usage spike or queue depth
- Wants “Is shadowing causing load?” “Are we dropping shadow runs?” “Do we need to kill-switch?”
3) Product/eng lead monitoring rollouts
- Wants “Are we meeting quality gate?” “Is canary halted?” “Where is it failing (region/route)?”

Information architecture (proposed)
A) Global navigation entry
- Console left nav: Rollouts → Shadow Evals
- Rationale: keeps it near A/B + canaries; users already associate “evaluation” with rollout confidence.

B) Two entry points (deep links)
1) Shadow Evals (global overview)
- For cross-route monitoring and triage.
- Default view: last 24h across routes the user has access to.
2) Route detail → tab: “Shadow Evals”
- For focused analysis while changing a single route’s model/version/prompt config.

C) Page structure
1) Header: scope + status
- Route selector (optional if in global view)
- Time range
- Baseline (primary) and Candidate (shadow target) selectors
- Policy summary chip(s): sampling %, allowlist, region constraints, retention mode (e.g., “Redacted”), and whether gates are active.
- System health chip(s): shadow queue health, drop rate, kill-switch status (only show if relevant and user has permission).

2) KPI strip (top)
- Quality (judge win-rate vs baseline)
- Safety pass-rate (policy outcomes)
- Format adherence rate (structured output / schema compliance)
- Output similarity (where configured)
- Latency delta (p50/p95) vs baseline
- Cost delta (tokens, $ estimate) vs baseline
- Sample size + confidence indicator (see ‘Stats / confidence UI’ below)

3) Time series section
- Primary: “Judge win-rate over time” (stacked win/lose/tie or win rate + CI)
- Secondary toggles: safety pass rate, format adherence, latency delta, cost delta
- Event overlays: rollout state changes (canary started/paused/held/rolled back), policy changes (sampling %, target changes), kill-switch toggles

4) Breakdown table
- Purpose: find where regressions cluster.
- Dimensions (ordered by usefulness; keep tight to avoid cardinality explosion):
  a) Region
  b) Model target (candidate identifier)
  c) Route / endpoint (if on global page)
  d) Error reason buckets (timeouts, budget drops)
  e) “Policy bucket” (sampling tier) — only if we can keep it low-cardinality
- Columns: win-rate, safety fail rate, format fail rate, latency delta p95, cost delta, shadow run completion rate, samples
- Click row → drill-down panel

5) Drill-down: examples (gated / permissioned)
- Panel with “Example comparisons” (N=20 default)
- Shows: prompt (redacted/hashed per policy), baseline output, candidate output, judge rationale (if enabled), tags (safety result, format result), timestamps
- Must include warning when examples are not stored due to customer retention/redaction settings.

Comparison model (baseline vs candidate)
- Baseline = primary production response (the one returned to end-user)
- Candidate = shadow target output
- IMPORTANT: Some customers will have multiple shadow targets simultaneously (e.g., candidate model + candidate quant profile). UI needs to scale beyond 1:1.

Proposal
1) Default mode: 1 baseline vs 1 candidate
- Two selectors in header.
- Baseline selector is often read-only on route pages (it’s “current primary config”), but selectable in global view.

2) Optional mode: multi-candidate comparison
- Toggle: “Compare multiple candidates”
- Chart becomes small multiples or layered series (limit to 3–5 candidates)
- Breakdown table adds candidate as first column and allows sorting by win-rate.
- Guardrail: hard cap number of candidates displayed (avoid unreadable chart + backend explosion).

Stats / confidence UI (must-have for beta)
- Show sample size everywhere (n)
- Add a “Data quality” indicator:
  - “Good” if n >= threshold and completion rate high
  - “Limited” if n below threshold
  - “Degraded” if many drops/timeouts/budget skips
- For win-rate: show confidence intervals (or at least a “±” band) and a tooltip describing judge variance.
- Copy: avoid stating “Model X is better” — prefer “Candidate is winning on sampled traffic” + link to methodology.

Customer-facing terminology (draft decisions)
Goal: be precise, but not scary. Avoid implying user traffic is being “replayed” in a way that affects users.

Recommended terms in UI
- Feature name: “Shadow Evals” (short, customer-friendly)
- System concept (docs/tooltips): “Shadow Traffic” (for technical accuracy)
- Baseline: “Primary”
- Candidate: “Shadow target” in technical contexts; “Candidate” in comparison contexts
- Sampling: “Sampling rate” (avoid “mirror percentage” in UI; we can mention mirroring in tooltip)
- Execution health: “Shadow completion rate” (avoid “drop” as primary label; use “dropped shadow runs” in tooltip)
- Storage: “Retention mode: Redacted/No payloads/Full payloads (restricted)” (final naming pending Security)

Terms to avoid (or use only in internal admin)
- “Replay” (implies later re-execution; we do mirror, but async)
- “Duplicate requests” (can raise customer fear about double billing / double side effects)
- “Secondary production” (confusing)

Copy notes (high-signal phrases)
- In header tooltip: “Shadow runs do not affect end-user responses. Shadow execution is asynchronous and may be skipped when capacity budgets are reached.”
- On cost: “Shadow runs incur additional compute and may be subject to quotas.” (tie to pricing/packaging later)

Metrics presentation notes (what customers actually understand)
Quality
- “Judge win-rate” needs a glossary panel:
  - What is being judged (candidate vs baseline)
  - What rubric is used (customer-configurable vs default)
  - That it’s a comparative signal, not ground truth
- Provide a second “simple” metric for non-ML users:
  - “Regression risk: Low/Medium/High” derived from gate thresholds + confidence + safety/format.

Safety
- Present as “Safety policy pass rate” with breakdown by policy category if available (e.g., “PII”, “self-harm”, “hate”).
- Avoid too many categories in first iteration; default to top 3 categories + “Other”.

Format adherence
- If route is configured for structured output / schema: “Schema adherence rate”
- If not: hide metric entirely (don’t show 100% by default; it confuses)

Latency/cost
- Show deltas vs baseline (candidate - baseline)
- Default: p50 + p95 latency delta; tokens delta and cost estimate delta
- Include “shadow queue time” in a tooltip for SREs, but not as default KPI.

Operational controls surfaced in UI (permissions-gated)
- Kill switch state (global + per-route). Show as read-only indicator for most roles; only admin can toggle.
- Budget status: “Shadow budget reached (runs skipped)” as an annotation.
- Rate limiting/backpressure: represent as “skipped due to budget” rather than “error” to reduce panic.

Filters / grouping (cardinality guardrails)
- Default filters:
  - Time range (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, custom)
  - Route
  - Region
  - Candidate
- Do NOT offer free-form tags, user_id, request_id filters in customer UI.
- If we need “customer allowlist” visualization: show as a count or named allowlist id, not raw customer ids.

Drill-down permissions & data handling
- Example comparisons panel should obey retention/redaction settings strictly.
- If payloads are not stored, show:
  - “Examples unavailable due to retention settings”
  - Still show aggregate metrics and health.
- If payloads are stored in restricted mode, add audit note (internal) and “export disabled” by default.

Beta UX: feature flags and progressive disclosure
- Beta label: “Beta” pill next to Shadow Evals.
- Progressive disclosure: hide advanced toggles (multi-candidate, category breakdowns) behind “Advanced” accordion.
- Provide “Methodology” side panel with:
  - what is sampled
  - how judging works
  - what happens when budgets are exceeded
  - how to interpret low sample sizes

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Where do we show rollout gating outcomes?
- Option A: Shadow Evals shows “Gate status: passing/failing” and links to Rollout detail.
- Option B: Rollout detail shows gate status; Shadow Evals stays metric-only.
- Lean: Option A (status is the #1 question during canary), but keep details in Rollout view.

2) Naming of “shadow target” vs “candidate configuration”
- Evals team prefers “target” (aligns with routing). Design prefers “candidate” (aligns with A/B mental model).
- Proposed: UI uses “Candidate”; tooltips/docs use “Shadow target (candidate configuration)”.

3) Judge model transparency
- Do we expose which judge model/version generated the score?
- For beta: show as tooltip + “judge config id” for power users; avoid front-and-center.

4) Examples sampling
- If we store examples, do we store only “interesting” ones (judge disagrees, safety fails) vs random?
- Proposal: default to stratified sampling: disagreements + failures + random baseline.

5) Cost attribution wording
- “Shadow usage” should be clearly separated from “Production usage”.
- Need alignment with PM-613; for now we’ll label as “Shadow compute estimate” and avoid billing language.

Wireframe notes (textual)
- Global page: a “Routes at risk” table at the top might be more valuable than a blank overview.
  - Columns: route, candidate, win-rate delta, safety delta, format delta, completion rate, last 1h samples
  - Clicking row takes you to route detail with selectors pre-filled.

Next steps / action items
- Kenji: draft wireframes for route detail Shadow Evals tab (v1) focusing on baseline vs candidate + time series + breakdown table.
- Alicia: propose visual language for confidence/sample-size (“n”, CI shading, data quality chip) and for annotations (policy change, rollout state).
- Marissa: align with Paula on where “gate status” lives and what copy to use when a rollout is auto-held.
- Chloe/Jin: confirm backend can support selectors + breakdowns (candidate list, region breakdown) without high-cardinality queries.
- Logan: confirm metric naming/availability for completion vs drop reasons to support “Data quality” chip.
- Jonas: provide short methodology blurb and glossary (judge, rubric, ties, calibration) for the side panel.

Decision log (current as of 2025-11-13)
- Use “Shadow Evals” as UI feature name; “Shadow Traffic” remains technical term in docs.
- Default comparison mode is 1 baseline vs 1 candidate; multi-candidate is “Advanced” and capped.
- Always show sample size; do not allow strong claims without confidence framing.
- Examples drill-down is optional and retention-dependent; dashboard must remain useful with aggregates only.

Notes to self (PM)
- Make sure we do not accidentally imply that shadow runs are billed the same as production until PM-613 is settled.
- Confirm whether “Primary response cost” is available for baseline in a way that’s comparable to shadow cost (same token accounting). If not, stick to candidate absolute cost + latency for beta.
